land.text: the Kathmandu Valley under the Malla dynasty

predecessors.note: The Kathmandu page: 'The Licchavi era was followed by the Malla era' (no year); the thakuri-dynasty dossier (another group) ends the Thakuris c. 1200 and hands the valley to this state. My pages do not name the Thakuris.

successors.note: 'After the fall of Kirtipur, Shah took the city-state of Kathmandu in 1768'; on 25 September 1768 he announced the Kingdom of Nepal; Lalitpur fell in 1768 and Bhaktapur in 1769. Cliopatria's Gorkha Kingdom shape of 1762-1768 already covers the valley (4 cells).

capitals.name: Kantipur (Kathmandu)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Basantapur'; the page puts the seat of Jayasthiti Malla's rule (1382-1395) at Bhadgaon (Bhaktapur) and does not label Kathmandu the capital; 'From ancient times until the medieval period, Kathmandu was known as Kantipur' (Kathmandu page). Coordinates approximate.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1201: the Malla dynasty's infobox says 'Established: c. 1201' (Arimalla 'reigned 1200-16'); Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1202. The outline used is the 1202 shape (the valley, 661 km2). [Reviewer sa-04-a: verdict ok to adjust: a new keyframe with from, to and a correction]

661 km2 (4 grid cells): the Kathmandu Valley with Patan, Bhaktapur and Banepa. The Kathmandu page's infobox gives 49.45 km2 for the city and 899 km2 for the metropolitan area (ratio 0.74 to the metro area, within a factor of two). The valley belongs to one Malla kingdom to 1482; after the division of 1482 'among Yaksha Malla's sons into Bhaktapur, Kantipur (Kathmandu), and Lalitpur (Patan)' the outline stays the whole valley because Cliopatria has no rows for Bhaktapur or Patan and the three kingdoms cannot be told apart on a 165 km2 grid cell. Valid for 1202-1699.

union.text: the hill fort of Nuwakot, north-west of the valley

correction.text: the valley plus the Nuwakot fort

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1700-1743: 'Nuwakot was under Kantipur's administrative control in 1700' ('Nara Bhupal Shah failed to invade Nuwakot in 1700'); it stays so until the Gorkhalis 'captured the hill fort on September 26, 1744'. Cliopatria's outline omits it.

635 km2: the valley outline loses one small area in 1744 (-26 km2), the year the Gorkhalis 'captured the hill fort' of Nuwakot; the page gives no valley land lost, and the 1745 attempt under Kashiram Thapa to retake Nuwakot failed. Unverified: the shape's change is below the grid cell.

714 km2, 79 km2 above the 1744 outline: no page explains the growth (the timeline's note that Nuwakot was 'returned to Kathmandu in 1745' contradicts the article's 'permanent control'). Unverified: page budget.

661 km2, the 1202 outline again for 1757-1761. 'In 1757, The Gorkhalis set up a base on Naikap to mount their assault on Kirtipur'; the timeline has a peace treaty between Gorkha and Kathmandu in 1758 (terms not given). Cliopatria ends the row in 1761, seven years before the fall of the city.

correction.text: the Kathmandu Valley unchanged to the fall of the city

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1762-1768: the Kathmandu row ends in 1761, but 'After the fall of Kirtipur, Shah took the city-state of Kathmandu in 1768' and Lalitpur the same year, Bhaktapur in 1769. Cliopatria's Gorkha shape of 1762 overlaps the valley (4 cells): the gorkha-kingdom dossier should remove it until 1768.

ledger.note: c. 1201: Arimalla founds the Malla dynasty of the valley. Infobox 'Established: c. 1201'; 'Arimalla (reigned 1200-16) was the first king to be so-called'. The page does not name his predecessors; the Kathmandu page has 'The Licchavi era was followed by the Malla era'.

1484: Ratna Malla makes Kathmandu a kingdom of its own. 'After 1482, a crucial date in Nepalese history, the kingdom was divided' among Yaksha Malla's sons (Bhaktapur, Kantipur, Lalitpur); 'Ratna Malla was the first to rebel against this system of joint rule, seizing Kathmandu in 1484' and ruled it alone to 1520. The Malla kingdom of the united valley becomes the Kingdom of Kantipur.

1597: Sivasimha Malla unites Patan with Kathmandu. Sivasimha Malla 'conquered it in 1597 and united it with Kathmandu'; the kingdoms 'were later separated again among grandsons' (no year). Patan lies inside the whole-valley outline at every date.

ledger.note: 1700: Nuwakot is a Kantipur dependency. 'Nuwakot was under Kantipur's administrative control in 1700'; the page does not say when it was acquired, so 1700 is the first year it is seen (confidence 1).

region.text: the hill fort of Nuwakot, north-west of the valley

ledger.note: 26 September 1744: the Gorkhalis storm Nuwakot, opening the war for the valley. They 'managed to capture the hill fort on September 26, 1744'; in 1745 Jaya Prakash Malla sent Kashiram Thapa to retake it and failed.

region.text: the hill fort of Nuwakot, north-west of the valley

ledger.note: 26 September 1744: Nuwakot falls to Gorkha. 'managed to capture the hill fort on September 26, 1744'; the timeline's 'returned to Kathmandu in 1745' contradicts the article's 'permanent control'.

union.text: the hill fort of Nuwakot, north-west of the valley

ledger.note: 25 September 1768: Prithvi Narayan Shah takes Kathmandu. 'After the fall of Kirtipur, Shah took the city-state of Kathmandu in 1768' and on 25 September 1768 announced the Kingdom of Nepal; Lalitpur falls the same year, Bhaktapur in 1769 ('completing his conquest of the Nepal Valley').

September 1768: the Kingdom of Kantipur ends. The Malla dynasty's infobox says 'Disestablished: 25 November 1769' (Bhaktapur); Kathmandu itself ended in 1768, 'the Malla confederation after the Battle of Kathmandu in 1768' (Kathmandu page).

wars.name: Gorkha conquest of the Kathmandu Valley

zones.text: the hill fort of Nuwakot, north-west of the valley

wars.outcome: Nuwakot taken 26 September 1744; Naikap base against Kirtipur 1757; peace treaty 1758; Kirtipur assaulted again in 1764 and captured in 1766 (timeline); Gorkha defeats a British force at Sindhuli in 1767 that came 'to help king of Kathmandu'; Kathmandu falls 1768, Lalitpur 1768, Bhaktapur 1769.
wars.note: The article's text and its timeline differ on the Kirtipur dates (1764 and 1767 against 1766).

wars.name: Sivasimha Malla's conquest of Patan
wars.outcome: 'conquered it in 1597 and united it with Kathmandu'; separated again later (no year).

certainty.note: The valley rim is a natural boundary, but no page gives a frontier; the shape is Cliopatria's single 661 km2 outline.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Kathmandu' row (1202-1761, Wikipedia title 'Kathmandu') is the whole Kathmandu Valley (661 km2, 4 grid cells) under the Malla dynasty; this dossier starts in 1201 (the Malla infobox's c. 1201) and ends in 1768 (the fall of the city to the Gorkhalis), not 1761: Cliopatria ends the row seven years early and its Gorkha shape from 1762 covers the valley (the gorkha-kingdom dossier, sa-05, should hold it back to 1768-1769). Pages opened: 3 of 5 (Kathmandu, Malla dynasty (Nepal), Unification of Nepal); the Kathmandu city page is nearly silent on dates. NOT SETTLED: (1) the three valley kingdoms of 1482-1768 (Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, Patan) cannot be drawn apart on a 165 km2 cell and Cliopatria has no rows for Bhaktapur or Patan; they need dossiers (kingdom-of-bhaktapur, kingdom-of-lalitpur) from group sa-05 or the additions batch, with the 1649 Banepa reincorporation (Bhadgaon) and Kirtipur; (2) the shapes of 1744, 1748 and 1757 differ by single cells and no page explains them; (3) the Patan union of 1597 and its undated separation 'among grandsons'; (4) Jayasthiti Malla's reunion 1382-1395 and Yaksha Malla (c. 1428-1482) are not events here (no change of shape); the 'capital' is Kantipur throughout although the page seats Jayasthiti Malla at Bhadgaon; (5) Nuwakot 1700-1744: acquisition undated; (6) timeline 'returned to Kathmandu in 1745' against 'permanent control' of the Gorkhalis. No ruler list is given: the pages name Arimalla (1200-16), Jayasthiti (1382-1395), Yaksha Malla (c. 1428-82), Ratna Malla (1484-1520), Pratap Malla (1641-74) and Jaya Prakash Malla (to 1768) only partly. Gazetteer: 'Nuwakot' and 'Kirtipur' are real places the gazetteer lacks and are left as names (Nuwakot is about 85.17E 27.91N).
